claims.statement: The DSH plugin exposes PowerContext model-facing operations only as native MCP tools named mcp__powercontext__<operation>; it registers no direct HTTP operation tools, and a tool name is accepted only when its suffix is in the generated MCP catalog.

registerMcp races the native MCP initialization against a 5000 ms deadline; if the deadline wins it logs mcp_connect as pending with recovery /pc doctor and returns, while the initialization promise is not cancelled and the native client keeps connecting and publishes tools later.

An MCP initialization failure is logged as mcp_connect and does not reject registration, and the MCP config sets failOnStartupError to false and toolCallTimeoutMs to 60000 so the host stays usable while the Server is unavailable.

The native DSH MCP client does not reach the Server directly: protectMcpEndpoint opens a relay on 127.0.0.1 with a random path that accepts only GET, POST and DELETE, rejects redirects, and replaces upstream HTTP error bodies with fixed error codes.

The tools/pre-execute policy denies unknown mcp__powercontext__ names, denies arguments containing likely secrets, denies a call when the host Scope cannot be resolved or the arguments do not use that Scope, and returns an approval request for every non-read-only catalog operation.

Resolved defaults are baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8000, allowInsecureHttp false, timeoutMs 4000, requestTimeoutMs 1000, maxBytes 8000, capturePrompts true, flushOnCapture false, flushMaxCalls 4, with scopeId and authorization unset by default.

Configuration precedence for capturePrompts and flushOnCapture is the environment variable POWERCONTEXT_DSH_CAPTURE_PROMPTS or POWERCONTEXT_DSH_FLUSH_ON_CAPTURE when set to a recognized boolean, otherwise the plugin patch value, otherwise the default; maxBytes outside 512 to 32768 is rejected.

The authorization is taken from POWERCONTEXT_DSH_AUTHORIZATION first, then the plugin patch, then the stored credential file under DSH_HOME; the stored file is ignored when its permissions grant group or other access on non-Windows, when its server_url does not match baseUrl, or when the value is not a single Bearer token.
The ownerLocal setting takes POWERCONTEXT_DSH_OWNER_LOCAL when set and otherwise the plugin patch ownerLocal; a non-boolean value fails configuration validation, and an unset value stays undefined.

Each model step runs the automatic pre-step: if the downstream pre-step throws, the error is rethrown with no PowerContext message appended; if the downstream decision is not enter, has no messages, or has no non-empty query, it is returned unchanged.
The automatic pre-step budget combines the host signal with AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs), and an already-aborted signal returns the downstream decision unchanged.

Scope for the pre-step is resolved every turn through resolve_scope_binding; if resolution throws or returns nothing, prepare, capture and flush are skipped, and an unresolved Scope returns the downstream decision without recall.

Context recall posts a body with scope_id, a query bounded to 8192 characters and bytes, max_bytes, and an optional assembly to POST /v1/context/prepare, and accepts only a strictly shaped prepared-context object whose status is ready with byte-exact content or empty with null content.

The user prompt is captured in the same pre-step, after the prepare request and before the model step, regardless of whether prepare produced content, unless the signal is aborted or the prompt is empty.

Prompt capture is skipped when capturePrompts is false, when the prompt exceeds 200000 characters, or when it contains the authorization value or a secret; otherwise it posts to POST /v1/sources/content with a source_id that is the SHA-256 of scope, session, turn and prompt, and the metadata origin dsh and event user_prompt_submit.

When flushOnCapture is enabled and the capture returns a valid source position, the plugin polls flush_memory up to flushMaxCalls times until current_cursor reaches that position; reaching it reports only that the cursor was reached, and running out of calls reports flush_budget_exhausted.

A failed prepare leaves the turn running as ordinary conversation with no PowerContext context content; the Scope routing message is still appended whenever the Scope resolved, and the downstream messages are otherwise returned unchanged.

Prepared context is appended as untrusted context that supersedes earlier PowerContext snapshots, and the Scope routing message states the host Scope is authoritative for mcp__powercontext__ operations.

The /pc command set (status, doctor, search, remember, flush, review, stats, capabilities, skills scan) calls the Server directly through the command handler and does not pass through the MCP tool policy; commands that need a Scope return unscoped when none resolves.

The owner-local deployment gate rejects a request in order: a non-loopback socket with local_only, an SSH launch with ssh_untrusted, then allows Desktop or ownerLocal true, rejects ownerLocal false with owner_local_disabled, and otherwise rejects with owner_local_unverified.

Desktop is identified by the managed desktop profile context name, not by Electron, and the SSH launch fact is read from SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY; resolveDeployment returns null when the host is SSH or is neither Desktop nor explicitly owner-local.
Loopback is the IPv4 127.0.0.0/8 range or ::1, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms; loopback alone is not treated as proof of a local owner.

The status and dashboard routes first apply the DSH connection rejection (401 or 403), then the owner-local gate, accept only GET (other methods get 405), and return status JSON with no-store headers.

The status bridge performs only read-only probes: get_liveness, get_server_info for the package version, get_readiness and get_capabilities; it never calls prepare, capture, generation, MCP or /pc doctor, and a failed liveness probe skips readiness and capabilities.
The sidebar routes are registered only when the host provides webServer and connection services; a headless host skips the registration so tools and hooks still load.

The dashboard route reads the Server's /dashboard/home once per request with a timeout between 1 and 8 seconds and reports disabled, authentication, load_unavailable, scope_unresolved, available, or server_unavailable states.
The /pc command set is registered under the pc name, and a Scope-less status call still reports the automatic-path status.

The internal LocalDeliveryService prepares handoff packages from inspected work, a configured generation, or an exact Handoff revision, and it does not add a browser route or enable delivery in the DSH UI on its own; recovery marks an interrupted delivery unknown rather than re-running the original Source.

The handoff package store keeps 100 carrier slots or 50 MiB by default, never evicts pending or pinned packages, keeps a 30-day tombstone after deletion, and can expire an unpinned confirmed package after seven days.
The dsh-pet companion applies only for the web or desktop profile when the host exposes its pet memory slot, and it registers a recall and capture provider in that slot.
dsh-pet recall runs a text search with limit 3 inside a 1200 ms budget, wraps the results as untrusted historical evidence capped at 3072 bytes, and backs off for five seconds after a failure.

dsh-pet captures each dialogue turn into a per-generation local queue and drains it through capture_content_source on a one-second tick with a five-second timeout; a successful capture is removed, a conflict or rejection blocks the item, and other failures retry with exponential backoff.

Pet memory bindings must be between one and sixteen unique PET_ID=SCOPE_ID pairs with a different existing Scope for each pet, and the setup flags --dsh-pet-memory on or off, --dsh-pet-bind and --discard-dsh-pet-pending are validated together.

Setup requires a built lib/index.js, stages the powercontext-project-context Skill, runs dsh plugin add for the selected profile, and defaults the profile to web; the Desktop profile requires the Desktop-installed dsh command.

The DSH verify step inspects only registration through dsh --profile web --dump-config and reports running host configuration, Server liveness and readiness, route compatibility and session Scope as not observed or not checked, leaving /pc doctor as the runtime check.
The HTTP client refuses unknown operation ids, sends requests with redirect set to manual, and gives the readiness operation at least a 40 second timeout.

Plugin installation writes the connection transport and then runs the installer's enable step when present, and a failure during setup is reported as a connection or native activation failure with the install already complete.
